legend: This lesion shows well-formed (although frequently angulated and irregular) vascular spaces lined by moderately atypical endothelial cells with areas of stratification and hobnailing. The surrounding stroma shows chronic inflammation with haemosiderin-laden macrophages.
source:
Prof Cyril Fisher MD DSc FRCPath Department of Musculoskeletal Pathology, University Hospitals Birmingham, Robert Aitken 
Institute for Clinical Research, University of Birmingham, Birmingham B15 2TT, UK.

legend: Although the neoplastic endothelial cells here show relatively minimal atypia, vasoformation is rudimentary, with small, poorly defined vascular channels containing erythrocytes.
source:
Prof Cyril Fisher MD DSc FRCPath Department of Musculoskeletal Pathology, University Hospitals Birmingham, Robert Aitken 
Institute for Clinical Research, University of Birmingham, Birmingham B15 2TT, UK

legend: Poorly defined vascular channels are lined by large, moderately pleomorphic cells with ovoid nuclei, with areas of stratification. There is prominent surrounding blood, with mixed inflammation and haemosiderin deposition.
source:
Prof Cyril Fisher MD DSc FRCPath Department of Musculoskeletal Pathology, University Hospitals Birmingham, Robert Aitken 
Institute for Clinical Research, University of Birmingham, Birmingham B15 2TT, UK

legend: This neoplasm has a predominantly solid architecture, with sparse vasoformation. The cells are large with moderately atypical vesicular nuclei and prominent nucleoli. Foci of rudimentary vasoformation with intracytoplasmic lumina are present.
source:
Prof Cyril Fisher MD DSc FRCPath Department of Musculoskeletal Pathology, University Hospitals Birmingham, Robert Aitken 
Institute for Clinical Research, University of Birmingham, Birmingham B15 2TT, UK

legend: This poorly differentiated angiosarcoma shows strong diffuse nuclear expression of ERG, the most sensitive and specific endothelial marker. Immunohistochemical confirmation of endothelial differentiation is critical for the diagnosis of tumours without discernible vasoformation.
source:
Prof Cyril Fisher MD DSc FRCPath Department of Musculoskeletal Pathology, University Hospitals Birmingham, Robert Aitken 
Institute for Clinical Research, University of Birmingham, Birmingham B15 2TT, UK
